title: Biological Technicians
description: Assist biological and medical scientists. Set up, operate, and maintain laboratory instruments and equipment, monitor experiments, collect data and samples, make observations, and calculate and record results. May analyze organic substances, such as blood, food, and drugs.

tasks.text: Conduct research, or assist in the conduct of research, including the collection of information and samples, such as blood, water, soil, plants and animals.
Use computers, computer-interfaced equipment, robotics or high-technology industrial applications to perform work duties.
Monitor and observe experiments, recording production and test data for evaluation by research personnel.
Analyze experimental data and interpret results to write reports and summaries of findings.
Provide technical support and services for scientists and engineers working in fields such as agriculture, environmental science, resource management, biology, and health sciences.
Keep detailed logs of all work-related activities.
Isolate, identify and prepare specimens for examination.
Set up, adjust, calibrate, clean, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory and field equipment.
Clean, maintain and prepare supplies and work areas.
Monitor laboratory work to ensure compliance with set standards.
Place orders for laboratory equipment and supplies.
Participate in the research, development, or manufacturing of medicinal and pharmaceutical preparations.
Conduct standardized biological, microbiological or biochemical tests and laboratory analyses to evaluate the quantity or quality of physical or chemical substances in food or other products.
Examine animals and specimens to detect the presence of disease or other problems.
Measure or weigh compounds and solutions for use in testing or animal feed.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: IBM Lotus 1-2-3, Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Microsoft .NET Framework.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: BD Biosciences CellQuest, BoxShade, ClustalW, Gene Codes Sequencher.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Photoshop, Graphics software, Harvard Graphics.
